faqItems.question: Is InstanceDeck free?
faqItems.answer: Yes. It is free and open source under the MIT license.

faqItems.question: Does it modify Claude, Codex or other apps?
faqItems.answer: No. InstanceDeck launches the official app with different launch settings and data folders. Nothing is patched, copied or repackaged, so the app's own updates keep working.

faqItems.question: Can I run two Claude Desktop accounts at the same time?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Each profile signs in once using the guided sign-in, then stays signed in. Your main Claude keeps working as before.

faqItems.question: Is this allowed by the apps’ terms?
faqItems.answer: InstanceDeck is meant for keeping accounts you own separate, such as work and personal. Do not use it to share accounts or to get around usage limits. Check each provider's terms for your situation. This is not legal advice.

faqItems.question: Where is my data stored?
faqItems.answer: On your PC, in a folder you choose. The default is %LOCALAPPDATA%\InstanceDeck\Profiles. Nothing is uploaded.

faqItems.question: Why does Windows show a SmartScreen warning?
faqItems.answer: InstanceDeck releases are unsigned, so Windows may warn or block installation. Verify the source and published SHA-256 checksums, and review the code signing policy before installing.

faqItems.question: Which apps are supported?
faqItems.answer: See the Apps directory. Each recipe shows its status and the versions it was tested on. Apps that accept a separate data path can be configured with a custom recipe.

faqItems.question: Is InstanceDeck affiliated with Anthropic or OpenAI?
faqItems.answer: No. It is an independent open-source project. Product names identify compatibility; they do not imply endorsement.

marketing.securityTitle: Designed to pass a security review.
marketing.securityBody: Profiles are isolation, not a sandbox. The threat model, every launch flag and the source are public, so your security team can check each claim.
